people.name: Queen Victoria
people.summary: British monarch (1837–1901); took over India from the Company (1858) and became Empress of India (1877).
facts: Her Proclamation of 1 November 1858 promised to respect Indian rulers and religions.
Proclaimed Kaiser-i-Hind (Empress of India) at the Delhi Durbar of 1877.
people.source: Standard modern Indian history (Spectrum / Bipan Chandra)

people.name: Dinabandhu Mitra
people.summary: Bengali playwright whose Nil Darpan (1860) exposed the cruelty of indigo planters.
facts: Wrote the play Nil Darpan ("Mirror of Indigo") in 1860.
Its English translation was published by Rev. James Long, who was jailed for it.
people.source: Standard modern Indian history (Spectrum / Bipan Chandra)

people.name: Jyotirao Phule
people.summary: Reformer who fought caste discrimination; founded the Satyashodhak Samaj and wrote Gulamgiri (1873) (NCERT).
facts: Said the "upper" castes had no right to land and power; the land belonged to the so-called low castes (NCERT).
Urged Shudras and Ati Shudras to unite against caste discrimination (NCERT).
Founded the Satyashodhak Samaj to spread caste equality (NCERT).
Wrote Gulamgiri (Slavery) in 1873 and dedicated it to the Americans who had fought to free slaves (NCERT).
With his wife Savitribai Phule opened a school for girls in Pune (1848).
people.source: NCERT Class 8 Our Pasts III, Ch. 7

people.name: Swami Dayananda Saraswati
people.summary: Founder of the Arya Samaj (1875), which tried to reform Hinduism (NCERT).
facts: Founded the Arya Samaj in 1875 (NCERT).
Supported widow remarriage (NCERT).
Gave the call "Back to the Vedas"; wrote Satyarth Prakash.
Started the Shuddhi movement.
people.source: NCERT Class 8 Our Pasts III, Ch. 7; Standard modern Indian history (Spectrum / Bipan Chandra)

people.name: Sayyid Ahmed Khan
people.summary: Founded the Mohammedan Anglo-Oriental College at Aligarh (1875) — the start of the Aligarh Movement (NCERT).
facts: Founded the MAO College at Aligarh in 1875; it later became Aligarh Muslim University (NCERT).
Offered modern education, including Western science, to Muslims (NCERT).
Founded the Scientific Society (1864) to translate Western works into Urdu.
people.source: NCERT Class 8 Our Pasts III, Ch. 7

people.name: Keshab Chandra Sen
people.summary: Brahmo leader who founded the Brahmo Samaj of India (1866) (NCERT shows him as a main Brahmo leader).
facts: One of the main leaders of the Brahmo Samaj (NCERT).
Split from Debendranath Tagore's Adi Brahmo Samaj and founded the Brahmo Samaj of India (1866).
Campaigned for the Native Marriage Act (1872), which allowed inter-caste marriage.
people.source: Standard modern Indian history (Spectrum / Bipan Chandra)

people.name: M.G. Ranade
people.summary: Judge and reformer; leading figure of the Prarthana Samaj and an early Congress leader.
facts: A leading member of the Prarthana Samaj (founded 1867 at Bombay).
Helped found the Poona Sarvajanik Sabha (1870).
Mentor of G.K. Gokhale.
people.source: Standard modern Indian history (Spectrum / Bipan Chandra)

people.name: Ram Singh Kuka
people.summary: Leader of the Namdhari (Kuka) movement in the Punjab; exiled to Rangoon (1872).
facts: Led the Namdhari (Kuka) movement, which preached a pure Sikhism and boycott of British goods and courts.
Exiled to Rangoon after the Kuka attacks of 1871–72.
people.source: Standard modern Indian history (Spectrum / Bipan Chandra)

images.credit: Style of Bishan Singh, possibly created by Kapur Singh of Amritsar / Wikimedia Commons

people.name: Lord Stanley
people.summary: First Secretary of State for India (1858).
facts: Became the first Secretary of State for India under the Government of India Act 1858.
people.source: Standard modern Indian history (Spectrum / Bipan Chandra)

people.name: Surendranath Banerjea
people.summary: Founder of the Indian Association (1876); twice Congress president; "Rashtraguru".
facts: Was dismissed from the ICS on a minor charge.
Founded the Indian Association with Ananda Mohan Bose in 1876.
Toured India against the lowering of the ICS age limit (1877).
Ran the newspaper The Bengalee.
Among the early Congress leaders named by NCERT; president of the INC in 1895 and 1902.
people.source: Standard modern Indian history (Spectrum / Bipan Chandra)

people.name: Courtenay Ilbert
people.summary: Law Member of the Viceroy's council who drafted the Ilbert Bill (1883).
facts: Drafted the bill to let Indian judges try European offenders (NCERT).

roles.title: Law Member, Viceroy's council
roles.appointedBy: the Secretary of State for India

people.source: Standard modern Indian history (Spectrum / Bipan Chandra)

people.name: William Wilson Hunter
people.summary: Chaired the Education Commission of 1882 under Ripon.
facts: Chaired the Hunter Commission on education (1882).
Compiled the Imperial Gazetteer of India.
people.source: Standard modern Indian history (Spectrum / Bipan Chandra)

people.name: Kandukuri Veeresalingam
people.summary: Telugu reformer who formed an association for widow remarriage (NCERT).
facts: Formed an association for widow remarriage in the Telugu-speaking areas of the Madras Presidency (NCERT).
Performed the first widow remarriage in Andhra at Rajahmundry (1881).
Started the journal Vivekavardhini (1874) and wrote the first Telugu novel, Rajasekhara Charitramu.
people.source: NCERT Class 8 Our Pasts III, Ch. 7; Andhra history

people.name: Helena Blavatsky
people.summary: Co-founder of the Theosophical Society (New York, 1875).
facts: Founded the Theosophical Society with Henry Olcott in New York (1875).
Moved its headquarters to Adyar, Madras (1882).
people.source: Standard modern Indian history (Spectrum / Bipan Chandra)

people.name: Henry Olcott
people.summary: Co-founder and first president of the Theosophical Society.
facts: Co-founded the Theosophical Society (1875) and settled at Adyar (1882).
people.source: Standard modern Indian history (Spectrum / Bipan Chandra)

images.credit: The original uploader was James.S at English Wikipedia. / Wikimedia Commons

people.name: A.O. Hume
people.summary: Retired British official who helped bring Indians together to form the Congress (1885) (NCERT).
facts: A retired British official (ICS) who played a part in bringing Indians from various regions together (NCERT).
Was the first General Secretary of the Congress.
people.source: Standard modern Indian history (Spectrum / Bipan Chandra)

people.name: W.C. Bonnerjee
people.summary: First president of the Indian National Congress (Bombay, 1885).
facts: Presided over the first session of the INC at Bombay (1885).
A Calcutta barrister; among the early leaders named by NCERT.
people.source: Standard modern Indian history (Spectrum / Bipan Chandra)

people.name: Bal Gangadhar Tilak
people.summary: Radical nationalist who declared "Freedom is my birthright and I shall have it!" (NCERT).
facts: Raised the slogan "Freedom is my birthright and I shall have it!" (NCERT).
Started public Ganapati (1893) and Shivaji (1895) festivals in Maharashtra.
Ran the newspapers Kesari (Marathi) and Mahratta (English).
Jailed for sedition in 1897 and sent to Mandalay (1908–14).
Started a Home Rule League in 1916.
people.source: Standard modern Indian history (Spectrum / Bipan Chandra)

people.name: Swami Vivekananda
people.summary: Disciple of Ramakrishna; spoke at the World Parliament of Religions, Chicago (1893); founded the Ramakrishna Mission (NCERT).
facts: His original name was Narendra Nath Dutta (NCERT).
Spoke at the World Parliament of Religions at Chicago in 1893 (NCERT).
Called people to rise above the "religion of the kitchen" and serve the nation (NCERT).
Founded the Ramakrishna Mission (1897), named after his guru, stressing salvation through social service (NCERT).
people.source: NCERT Class 8 Our Pasts III, Ch. 7

images.credit: The original uploader was Dziewa at English Wikipedia. / Wikimedia Commons

people.name: Ramakrishna Paramhansa
people.summary: Mystic of Dakshineswar; guru of Swami Vivekananda (NCERT).
facts: Taught that all religions lead to God.
The Ramakrishna Mission is named after him (NCERT).
people.source: NCERT Class 8 Our Pasts III, Ch. 7

people.name: Gurajada Apparao
people.summary: Telugu playwright and poet; wrote Kanyasulkam (1892) and the patriotic poem "Desamunu Preminchumanna".
facts: Kanyasulkam (1892) attacked the custom of selling young girls in marriage (bride price).
Pioneered spoken (vyavaharika) Telugu in literature.
Wrote "Desamunu Preminchumanna" — love the country, not just its soil.
people.source: Standard modern Indian history (Spectrum / Bipan Chandra)

people.name: Mortimer Durand
people.summary: Foreign Secretary who drew the Durand Line with Afghanistan (1893).
facts: Negotiated the Durand Line with Amir Abdur Rahman (1893).
people.source: Standard modern Indian history (Spectrum / Bipan Chandra)

people.name: Chapekar brothers
people.summary: Damodar and Balkrishna Chapekar shot the plague commissioner Rand at Poona (1897).
facts: Killed W.C. Rand, head of the harsh plague committee, and Lt Ayerst on 22 June 1897.
Were caught and hanged (1898–99).
people.source: Standard modern Indian history (Spectrum / Bipan Chandra)

people.name: Birsa Munda
people.summary: Munda leader who wanted to drive out missionaries, moneylenders, landlords and the government and set up a Munda Raj (NCERT).
facts: Born in the mid-1870s; grew up around the forests of Bohonda (NCERT).
Urged the Mundas to give up liquor, clean their villages and stop believing in witchcraft (NCERT).
Talked of a golden age (satyug) when Mundas lived a good life (NCERT).
Arrested in 1895 and jailed for two years; released in 1897 (NCERT).
His followers raised the white flag as a symbol of Birsa Raj (NCERT).
Died of cholera in 1900 (NCERT).
Jharkhand was formed on his birth anniversary, 15 November 2000.
people.source: NCERT Class 8 Our Pasts III, Ch. 4 "Tribals, Dikus and the Vision of a Golden Age"

people.name: Rabindranath Tagore
people.summary: Poet and Nobel laureate (1913) who led the Swadeshi protests of 1905 with songs and Raksha Bandhan.
facts: Wrote "Amar Sonar Bangla" during the protests of 1905 (now Bangladesh's national anthem).
Organised Raksha Bandhan as a symbol of Bengali unity on 16 October 1905.
Won the Nobel Prize for Literature for Gitanjali (1913).
Wrote Jana Gana Mana, first sung at the Calcutta Congress (1911).
Gave up his knighthood after Jallianwala Bagh (1919).
people.source: Standard modern Indian history (Spectrum / Bipan Chandra)
